input.standard: ASTM E741 (concentration decay, single zone); ASTM D6245 (occupant CO2 as tracer)
input.purpose: Measure V_lab, the volume of air the Lab scrubber serves, from a short reduced-speed rise then a full-speed decay, with the Lab's occupants as the CO2 source.

steps.why: Rise: reduced effective flow (0.4 m3/min) so the Lab's CO2 climbs several hundred ppm above sensor noise; short enough to end well under the working limit.
Decay: full speed (Qe 1 m3/min), about one time constant (V/Qe ~ 30 min for a first guess of 30 m3); fit C(t)=Ceq+(C0-Ceq)exp(-t/tau), V=Qe*tau.

abort.when: CO2 at or above limits.co2AbortPpm (3000 ppm) at any time; also end the rise early and go to step 2 if it reaches co2MaxPpm (2800 ppm)
the device refuses a step's command
battery state of charge under 35 percent
a monitored occupant leaves the 45-120 bpm band, monitoring is lost, or one more person enters the Lab

monitoring.reason: The test raises the CO2 of the air the two Lab occupants breathe; the monitor is simulated, not live.

expected.rise: Starting near 1550 ppm, Lab CO2 rises by roughly 300-500 ppm over 20 min (about 0.76 L/min from two awake occupants into ~30 m3 at 0.4 m3/min effective flow) and stays under 2800 ppm; a rise under ~100 ppm (noise level) or over 2800 ppm would show the source, the volume or the flow is not as assumed.
expected.decay: At full speed CO2 falls toward a lower equilibrium (about 760 ppm above outdoor air) with tau = V/Qe; for a first guess of V=30 m3, tau is about 30 min; the fit gives V_lab = 1 m3/min * tau, expected in 10-60 m3. A fit with tau much longer than the phase or a poor residual shows the hypotheses do not hold.
expected.hab_b: Hab-B CO2 stays flat with the hatch closed; a drift correlated with the Lab's shows exchange through the opening.
expected.commands: Both speed commands are accepted; the scrubber follows with its 3.33 min lag, so the first ~10 min of each phase are excluded from the fit.

hypotheses: The Lab is one well-mixed zone; the hatch is held closed for the whole test and the exchange with Hab-B through it is not measured, not assumed zero (design flow 3 m3/min is with hatch closed per station-topology; Hab-B CO2 is recorded to reveal it).
The two Lab occupants stay awake at constant activity (0.38 L/min each) and no one enters or leaves.
The scrubber's effective flow at 100 percent is 1 m3/min and scales with speed; lag 3.33 min.
The starting CO2 (1550 ppm) is already elevated, so the outdoor/background level is not the fit's asymptote: the fit is towards C_eq.
